text:
jordan_customer: Hey, streaming API is cutting off responses for us about 95% of the time. Final JSON chunk missing and finish_reason is absent. We get a valid stream for ~20s then nothing. Need urgent help, this breaks our product flow. request id: rq_7f4b9c (approx).

maria_support: Sorry you're hitting this, Jordan. Can you paste the exact curl/SDK request you used and a snippet of the raw SSE output? Also the request id + approximate timestamps helps.

jordan_customer: Here's a minimal curl we used to repro.
```bash
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" \n  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \n  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=redwood-large&prompt=..."
```
Raw tail of response we captured (truncated):
```
event: message
data: {"token":"...","text":"..."}

event: message
data: {"token":"","text":""}

event: message
data: {"token":"...","text":"more text"}

event: message
data: {"token":"...","text":"almost done"}

event: message
data: {"token":"","text":""}

# then connection closes abruptly, no final event, no finish_reason, no closing JSON brace
```

alex_engineer: Thanks — that looks like the connection was closed mid-stream. Can you confirm if you are behind any proxy/CDN (Cloudflare, Fastly) or corporate gateway? Also does the client reconnect or try to resume?

jordan_customer: We're on AWS ALB + nginx sidecars. Client does attempt a naive reconnect but the SDK's resume isn't working because the final chunk with the model's finish_reason and final tokens isn't present.

sam_sre: Two likely causes: 1) upstream proxy or ALB idle timeout closing socket before the server sends final flush, 2) buffering at nginx/fastly causing final bytes to be dropped on abrupt client disconnect. Do you have tcpdump/pcap or any proxy logs around 2026-02-12T14:22:11Z?

jordan_customer: I don't have packet capture yet. ALB logs show a 502 around that time for rq_7f4b9c. nginx logs show client terminated connection: "upstream prematurely closed connection".

maria_support: That log snippet is super helpful. Can you try a quick workaround: force smaller flush intervals / disable buffering on the server side, or set Connection: close as a test? If that helps, it's a proxy/timeout issue.

alex_engineer: Additional repro steps we recommend: 1) run the same request with curl -v to see the TCP teardown, 2) hit the hosted endpoint directly bypassing ALB (if possible) to see if it completes, 3) add server-side final flush sentinel like an explicit empty event with finish_reason to guarantee the tail is emitted.

sam_sre: For nginx specifically try adding headers: "X-Accel-Buffering: no" and ensure "proxy_buffering off; proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_set_header Connection ''" to avoid nginx buffering. ALB has a 60s idle timeout by default; if your stream has a long pause at the end the ALB may close it.

jordan_customer: Quick test: added X-Accel-Buffering: no on our sidecar and hit the endpoint again — stream stayed alive longer but still cut at ~24s. Curl -v shows FIN from ALB.

alex_engineer: Okay that points to ALB timeout. Two options: a) increase ALB idle timeout / keepalive, b) change server to emit a periodic keepalive event (a lightweight SSE comment or heartbeat) so ALB sees activity. Example heartbeat: "event: ping\ndata: {}\n\n" every 15s. That prevents ALB from thinking connection is idle.

jordan_customer: We tried periodic comment keepalive and the stream completed reliably for a few runs. Looks promising. Is this something we need Redwood to change server-side for long-term?

maria_support: We'll escalate. For a permanent fix our runtime team can: 1) ensure final events are flushed immediately and 2) emit a final sentinel chunk with finish_reason that is idempotent (so resuming clients can detect end even if they missed it).

alex_engineer: Internally, runtime change options: - flush final buffers synchronously before server-side connection close - add explicit end-of-stream event: {"type":"__end__","finish_reason":"stop"} - expose stream-heartbeat config to clients so we can server-side maintain small heartbeats if ALB present.

sam_sre: I'll open an infra ticket to audit ALB settings for customers using sidecars and publish recommended config. Temporary mitigations for customers: increase ALB idle timeout, enable keepalive heartbeats, and turn off nginx proxy buffering.

maria_support: Jordan — escalating to eng-runtime. Ticket INF-9123 created and linked: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-9123. Eng will prioritize a fix and a docs page with guidance for proxies (ALB/nginx/Cloudflare) and recommended headers and heartbeat examples.

jordan_customer: Thanks team, heartbeat workaround looks like it unblocks us. Please keep me posted on ETA for the runtime fix — this needs to be stable at scale.

alex_engineer: Noted. We'll track in INF-9123 and post updates here. Quick note: if you build resume logic, use the server-supplied final token index to avoid duplicates on reconnect; but our plan is to avoid requiring clients to handle missing final-chunk cases.

infra_bot: [INF-9123] created by maria_support assigned to alex_engineer. Priority: P2.

maria_support: Marking thread for follow-up in 48h after eng triage. :thumbsup:
